rounds.hypothesis: Per diagnose.json: sys_fsync/sys_fdatasync gate only on `as_inode_handle_or_err()`, which catches sockets but not pipes/FIFOs because both are InodeHandles in Asterinas, so the call falls through to the no-op default `Inode::sync_all`. The veto belongs in the per-open file description layer (PerOpenFileOps), which is where Asterinas already places the analogous `check_seekable` ESPIPE veto that PipeHandle overrides.
rounds.change: Added `PerOpenFileOps::check_syncable() -> Result<()>` with a default of `Ok(())` (kernel/src/fs/file/inode_handle.rs, next to `check_seekable`). Overrode it in `PipeHandle` (kernel/src/fs/pipe/common.rs) to return EINVAL. Added `InodeHandle::sync_all`/`InodeHandle::sync_data` plus a private `InodeHandle::check_syncable` that rejects `rights.is_empty()` with EBADF, then consults `open_file.check_syncable()`, then delegates to the inode via `path()`. Rewrote sys_fsync/sys_fdatasync to call those two methods instead of `as_inode_handle_or_err()?.path().sync_all()/sync_data()`. Uncommented fsync03 at test/initramfs/src/conformance/ltp/testcases/all.txt:450.
rounds.outcome: green on the first run: qemu.log line 43 'fsync03: pass (0.000s)', 5 passed / 0 failed / 0 broken, 'All conformance tests passed.' A second confirmation boot over the enabled neighbours on this code path (fsync02, fsync03, fdatasync01, msync01, msync02, pipe01, pipe02, pipe03, pipe11, open01, openat01) reported 90 passed / 0 failed / 0 broken.

layer: The per-open file description layer, matching diagnose.json's `owning_layer`: the veto is a new `PerOpenFileOps::check_syncable` method, dispatched from an `InodeHandle` method that both syscalls now route through. This layer owns the invariant because in Asterinas the decision 'does this file description have anything to make durable' is a property of the open file object, not of the inode: an anonymous pipe and a named FIFO share one `PipeHandle` per-open type but sit on different inodes (AnonPipeInode on PipeFs vs. a ramfs/ext2 NamedPipe inode), so a single per-open override covers both, while an inode-type check would need to be repeated in every filesystem that can host a FIFO.
generalizes: The rule is stated once and reached by every caller of the gate rather than by the path fsync03 walks. Concretely: (1) fdatasync gets the same fix for free. fsync03 never calls fdatasync, so a fix in sys_fsync alone would have left `fdatasync(pipe_fd)` still returning 0; both syscalls now go through `InodeHandle::sync_data`/`sync_all`, which share the same `check_syncable`. (2) Both pipe flavours are covered by the one override: the anonymous pipe (assertion 1) and the O_WRONLY FIFO (assertion 5) are the same `PipeHandle`, and so are the FIFO read end, the O_RDWR FIFO, and a FIFO on ext2 or virtiofs, none of which the test supplies. (3) The EBADF-on-O_PATH check closes an adjacent divergence diagnose flagged but fsync03 does not exercise: fsync/fdatasync on an O_PATH fd returned 0 and now returns EBADF, matching the host probe and the `rights.is_empty()` guard that 12 other InodeHandle operations already apply. (4) No branch anywhere tests the flag, size, or errno fsync03 happens to use; the pipe override is unconditional and does not inspect access mode, named-vs-anonymous, or status flags. Nothing regresses on the other side of the gate: the trait default is `Ok(())`, so all 13 other PerOpenFileOps implementors (devices, procfs, virtiofs, pty, evdev) keep their current behaviour, and files with no per-open object at all - regular files and directories - still delegate straight to the inode, which is why fsync02/fdatasync01 and the fs regression fdatasync test still pass. The remaining known gap is deliberate and recorded: Linux returns EINVAL for /dev/null and other device files whose fops carry no .fsync, whereas the `Ok(())` default keeps those at 0. Flipping the default to EINVAL would be closer to Linux but would change many device and pseudo-file paths at once, so it belongs in a separate change. sys_msync is unaffected either way - it calls `inode.sync_all()` directly, not through InodeHandle, and discards the result.
fix_summary: fsync/fdatasync on a pipe or FIFO now fail with EINVAL instead of silently returning success, and on an O_PATH descriptor fail with EBADF. The fix is designed against Asterinas' `PerOpenFileOps` trait - its analogue of Linux's `struct file_operations`, documented at inode_handle.rs:31-34 as the counterpart of Linux's `file_private` - rather than transplanting Linux's structure. Linux expresses the rule as the *absence* of an `.fsync` member in `pipefifo_fops`, which generic VFS code in fs/sync.c detects and turns into -EINVAL. Asterinas' trait has no notion of an absent method, so the equivalent is an explicit veto predicate, and the trait already carries exactly this shape in `check_seekable` (PipeHandle overrides it for ESPIPE). `check_syncable` is added alongside it and dispatched from new `InodeHandle::sync_all`/`sync_data` methods that mirror `InodeHandle::seek`: check rights first, consult the per-open object when one exists, then fall back to the inode. Routing both syscalls through those methods is what makes the single rule cover fdatasync and every future caller, and is what moves the O_PATH rights check onto the sync path, which previously bypassed InodeHandle entirely by reaching for `path()` directly.
